channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: Europae Laeva: States move to end Palantir contracts, but data access stays a vendor promise
item.description: The head of the Bundeswehr's cyber troops says Maven is not an option for Germany, and courts and governments across Europe have ended or set end-dates on Palantir work in recent years, with contracts there and in the UK worth more than €1.4 billion. The Bundeswehr is testing about 30 European systems, and the challenger's claim of full sovereignty is so far untested in public.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Europe's own battlefield AI exists. Our ministries should buy it now.
item.description: Helsing's Clarity does what NATO once bought from America, with the decision kept in human hands. Waiting past the Bundeswehr's own 2027 deadline is not prudence, so fund the finalists and let performance pick the winner.

item.title: Europae Dexter: US Treasury Secretary Bessent moves to military base over Iranian death threats
item.description: Iran has warned Europe that any part in the US blockade of its economy will be treated as an act of war, and US refuelling tankers have been diverted from RAF Mildenhall in England. Prosecutors have charged three men accused of acting for Iran in a plot against RAF Fairford.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US Treasury Secretary moves to military base after death threats linked to Iran
item.description: The United States has also moved refuelling aircraft from a British air base to Germany and other locations, and charged three men accused of plotting an attack on another British base on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

item.title: Europa Surgit: One attack hit eight countries. Europe needs one shield, not twenty-seven.
item.description: Hackers shut down supermarket refrigeration from Palermo to Helsinki, and each capital answered alone. Italy's Sala Cyber blocked 630,000 malicious events, and the EU foreign ministers in Brussels on Monday can extend the Tallinn Mechanism so it shields every member state.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Europe guards its ministries and leaves its food to hackers
item.description: The state intercepted 3.5 million malicious emails for the foreign ministry while supermarkets were broken into through open doors the government itself named. We pay twice, in spoiled food and in fear.

item.title: Europae Dexter: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard cyber unit for October attack, plans sanctions
item.description: Paris says the operation against French refrigeration systems was unprecedented in scale, and chief prosecutor Laure Beccuau is seeking international arrest warrants. ENISA warns its planned doubling of resources would never be enough.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyber attack on 700 retail sites
item.description: Paris will propose further sanctions against Iranian entities to its European partners. A Commission spokesperson said it is not the Commission's role to attribute cyber incidents. Iran rejects the accusations, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants.

item.title: Leo Batavus: EU auditors say uneven enforcement blunts Russia sanctions
item.description: Direct trade with Russia fell from 253 billion euros to 58 billion between 2021 and 2025. The European Court of Auditors calls for clearer rules and stronger monitoring, saying the Commission lacks criteria to judge whether the sanctions work.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU sanctions cut Russia trade to 58 billion euros but enforcement lags
item.description: Trade fell from 253 billion euros in 2021. The European Court of Auditors says unclear rules and uneven application let firms bypass the bans, and Russia now trades more with India and China.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Up to 50 leaders join Rutte in Dublin in Garda's biggest operation, say Gardaí
item.description: More than 5,000 Gardaí will work over 15,000 twelve-hour tours for the summit, while protesters march on Friday over fuel prices and the cost of living.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Garda call Dublin summit security operation largest in state's history
item.description: Mark Rutte joins up to 50 European leaders for the ninth European Political Community summit as officials brace for hoax threats and cyber attacks.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Rutte says Spain and Portugal treat Ukraine war as a distant Polish concern
item.description: The NATO Secretary General said a Russian missile takes five minutes longer to reach Lisbon than Warsaw. Portugal's foreign ministry, led by Paulo Rangel, called the remark light treatment of a serious matter.

item.title: Europae Dexter: A sanction Russia can shop around is not a sanction, it is a leak
item.description: The Court of Auditors found that enforcement varies by capital and companies pick the weakest border. The EU pays the full cost of the embargo and delivers only part of the pressure, so enforcement must move to Brussels.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Portugal rebukes NATO chief Rutte over 'flippant' missile remarks
item.description: The foreign ministry in Lisbon objected to remarks suggesting the government downplays the Russian threat, as Spain stayed silent.

item.title: Attacotti: ESET links Cereal email malware found at Romanian agency to Russia-aligned Turla
item.description: The security firm says the toolset, run on Microsoft Exchange, was set up to collect emails involving NATO and EU addresses. A Kazakh government body was also compromised, and ESET reads that hit as surveillance of Russian dissidents.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Slovak security firm links new email espionage tool to Russian hacking group Turla
item.description: ESET says the tool, found on a compromised Exchange server at a governmental organisation in Romania, was set to flag NATO and EU email traffic. A second victim in Kazakhstan was also identified.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Launch the Black Sea mission while Turla sits in government mail
item.description: A toolset built to filter NATO and EU correspondence sat on a Romanian government server, and Romania has asked for exactly this mission. Europe's governments should launch it and pay for cyber defence of ports and shipping lanes inside it.

item.title: Europae Laeva: British police arrest serving US soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old was held under the National Security Act near Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters in Gloucestershire, and faces possible charges from both Britain and the US Army.

item.title: Attacotti: US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old was detained near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023 and remains in custody at a London police station. The FBI director said the case involves allegations of espionage, which can carry a life sentence before an American military court.

item.title: Europa Surgit: US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: Counter Terrorism Policing detained the 41-year-old near Gloucester on 10 November under the National Security Act 2023, with police and the FBI working together on the case.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: French cyber agency blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for shop fridge attack
item.description: The cyberattack forced refrigeration at about 700 retail sites into high temperatures and destroyed the stock. The agency will ask European partners for new sanctions on Iranian entities.

item.title: Europa Surgit: EIB and investors pledge €10bn for European scale-ups
item.description: Seven member states and the EIB Group agreed the first closing of the Tech Champions fund-of-funds, aiming to mobilise up to €80 billion in venture capital.

item.title: Europae Laeva: EU and investors pledge over €10 billion to help European tech firms grow global
item.description: The EIB Group, 15 institutional investors and seven member states have pledged over €10 billion and hope to mobilise up to €80 billion in total, from a first closing of around €2 billion. The money is a pledge, not cash, and the European Commission calculated EU venture funding was about 84 percent below the American level in 2024.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US, Ukraine and Russia open first talks since February in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate two days of talks on security guarantees and territory, while Russian officials keep European representatives out of the main negotiations.

item.title: Europa Surgit: AfD split over ICE criticism as Chrupalla clashes with Weidel
item.description: Chrupalla calls for broader support on migration policy, while Tritschler pushes to copy US deportations. The dispute could shape whether Remigration stays a campaign theme.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Hackers hit freezers at 700 French supermarkets, Paris blames Iran
item.description: France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre named Iran's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit in a report on Monday. One German store owner says he threw away goods worth over 360,000 euros.

item.title: Leo Batavus: French minister Barrot calls Mélenchon a spokesman for the Kremlin
item.description: The foreign minister said Mélenchon's call for a vote in Donbas disqualifies him from office, and argued the EU budget, not French taxpayers, should carry the cost of backing Ukraine.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Crowd attacked National Guard base near Kyiv after torture-chamber fakes
item.description: Police used tear gas after about 200 people attacked a National Guard facility. Officials say the building was housing, not a prison, and Polish-language outlets spread the false claims.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Karasin says no agreement exists for Europeans to join the Abu Dhabi talks
item.description: Karasin called French plans of attendance wishful thinking, while Kallas says any agreement the EU is not party to will not be implemented. Costa has put EU participation on the agenda of Friday's informal leaders' meeting in Dublin.
